title.narrative: Rädda Barnen – Social sammanhållning, fredsbyggande och motståndskraft 2021–2024
Save the Children - Social Cohesion, Peace Building and Resiliency 2021-2024

description.narrative: Insatsen ämnar förbrättra lokala samhällen sociala sammanhållning, välmående och förmåga att återintegrera utsatta pojkar och flickor som riskerar att associeras eller som har anknytning till väpnade grupper genom tillhandahållandet av sociala skyddsnät, utbildning, försörjning samt civil-militär koordinering.

The intervention aims to improve the social cohesion, well-being and capacity of local communities to reintegrate vulnerable boys and girls at risk of association or associated with armed groups through the provision of social protection, education, livelihoods and civil-military coordination.

The overall objective of the program is to improve community level social cohesion, well-being and reintegration of vulnerable boys and girls at risk or associated with armed groups through integrated gender responsive, disability inclusive child protection, livelihood (CVA) and education services
The proposed program will achieve the following four key results:
Result 1. Vulnerable boys and girls affected by conflict and insecurity improve their safety and well-being through better, more equitable and inclusive access to comprehensive and conflict-sensitive child protection services.
Result 2. Vulnerable IDP and host community households are resilient and meet their basic needs through improved access to economic, food, life skills and community capacity building opportunities.
Result 3. Children (girls and boys) from communities affected by the security crisis have access to inclusive quality education in a safe and protective environment through capacity building in emergency education and psychological first aid.
Result 4. Community cohesion, child protection practice, and civil-military coordination is increased in order to facilitate programmes and protection of children and civilians affected by armed conflict.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
* During the implementation of the project, 2 545 households, including 1 782 households with internally displaced people and 763 vulnerable households, were assisted in the form of unconditional cash transfers or monthly food support. Additionally, 150 children benefited from individual case management, including cash transfers. According to the testimonies collected from beneficiaries, the cash enabled them to recover their dignity and ensure better living conditions for their children. According to the results of the various surveys analysed, the cash received has enabled beneficiaries to meet their food needs, provide health care for their children, and pay rent.
* Initially, the above mentioned households were planned to continue to receive cash grants. However, because of the Burkina Faso government suspension of all cash transfer programs mid-project, Save the Children had to swiftly adapt to new circumstances and replace the cash transfer program with monthly food support. This was successfully implemented.
* To promote the socioeconomic empowerment of vulnerable households, the approach consisted in identifying, among the cash transfer and/or food recipients, households capable of undertaking an income generating activity (IGA). The income generating activities undertaken by the beneficiaries enabled them to free themselves from humanitarian dependence and become economically independent. Through the economic activities they carry out, they are able to adequately meet their family's expenses. According to the testimonies of some beneficiaries, the savings generated through their activities have enabled them to ensure their children's schooling, acquire hygiene kits and meet their children's health needs.
* 150 young people received vocational training including a business installation kit in order set up their own business, make a salary and become independent. The program included training in sewing, tailoring, herding, farming etc. Of the young people trained, 77% could create their own business after the program.
* 13 temporary learning spaces have been constructed and equipped with school materials, resulting in that 1 654 students (including 1 346 internally displaced children) could continue attend school in a safe and protected environment. School kits were distributed to 9 949 students. This lead to a significant improvement in school performance.
* 61 instructors in the police, army and gendarmerie where trained on the rights and protection of children affected by the security crisis. These instructors in turn instructed more than 3 100 officers from the military, police and security domains. The training included relevant legal frameworks and humanitarian principles.
